messages:
jess_support: FYI multiple customers hitting p99 spikes / queueing since ~08:15 UTC, seeing 504s and delayed responses. Customer example attached with headers and trace id.

kai_oncall: noted, pulling graphs now - busy with another incident but can look. link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/cluster1?panel=p99_lat

riley_sre: saw the alert at 08:18. Inflight requests at worker-pool level are pegged at 100% for cluster1, admission rejects spiking. p95 up from 120ms -> 2s, p99 up to ~8s.

omar_eng-runtime: we pushed a small admission-control refactor in canary at 07:50 that changed token accounting and auth retry behavior. rolling back to verify. config diff (canary):
```
- admission_policy: token_bucket_v2
- max_tokens_per_worker: 64
+ admission_policy: token_bucket_v2_debug
+ max_tokens_per_worker: 128
+ auth_retry_on_429: true
```

jess_support: customer repro steps attached: repeated chat.generate calls (sync), many with streaming=false, token lengths ~400. They hit 504s and then retry.

kai_oncall: quick mitigations we can do: 1) temporarily increase global concurrency cap for cluster1, 2) enable emergency shedder to prioritize paying tenants, 3) rollback canary. I'll try 1 and 3 now.

deploy-bot: autoscaler: scaling up cluster1-workers +4 nodes (expected ~40s).

riley_sre: also seeing auth service returning intermittent 429s to runtime at ~08:11-08:16 which combined with auth_retry_on_429=true causes extra inflight retries, amplifying backpressure.

omar_eng-runtime: that's the root cause then. auth 429 -> runtime retries -> holds KV cache slots and admission tokens longer. I'll cut the retry flag and roll the canary back.

omar_eng-runtime: rollback started: reverting admission config to previous stable.

deploy-bot: deploy: rollback admission-control-canary -> success (rollout id: r-20260308-07-50)

kai_oncall: emergency shedder enabled for cluster1: priority-tenant routing active (top 10 paying accounts).

riley_sre: after rollback + scale, p95 down to ~180ms, p99 down to ~900ms. inflight back to normal. still monitoring.

jess_support: I'll update customers: primary account (acct-913) notified, offered 10% credit for the window.

maya_cust-success: sending note now, will follow up with postmortem invite.

omar_eng-runtime: root cause summary: canary enabled auth_retry_on_429=true which made transient auth throttles produce retries at runtime holding admission tokens -> queue pileup. Fixes: revert flag, add circuit-breaker on auth 429s, and add metrics to surface retry amplification.

kai_oncall: actions/tickets: INF-3421 for runtime circuit-breaker + metrics, INF-3422 to harden admission token accounting, and customer followups in CS-1298. I'll keep this thread updated if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

jess_support: closing loop for now, will re-open if customers still see p99 spikes. Thanks everyone. :pray:
